newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Alcorn, Basic get new contracts.
newsitem.headline: Alcorn, Basic get new contracts.

text.p: The Department of Energy (DOE) said on Monday it had signed a geophysical and exploration contract with a consortium led by Alcorn Petroleum and Minerals Co to explore for petroleum in the southern Philippines.
The contract calls for Alcorn to conduct 150 kms (95 miles) of seismic survey in the Agusan-Davao basin, spending about $100,000 during the first year and $200,000 in the second year.

Alcorn runs the West Linapacan field in the southwestern Philippines. The field has been plagued by water intrusion problems which cut output to 1,000 barrels per day from 18,000. The consortium decided to stop production in January.
The DOE said it was also scheduled to sign on Monday a similar deal with Basic Petroleum and Minerals Inc covering the Lingayen Gulf in the northern Philippines.
Basic is required to conduct a minimum 200 km (125 miles) of seismic survey at a cost of $200,000. It also has the option to drill two wells.
